record_id,Stable identifier for one included study.,"Assign the next unused identifier, starting with R001. Keep an existing study identifier unchanged when sorting or correcting the form. Additional arms, outcomes, periods, or companion reports do not receive separate study identifiers.","R followed by a positive integer, padded to three digits only when needed: R001 to R999, then R1000 onward. column1: eppi_record_id,Identifier for the included record in EPPI-Reviewer.,"Enter the identifier supplied from EPPI-Reviewer and retain it as text. The review author supplies future identifiers. Use N/A only when the study has no EPPI record. Do not invent an identifier or substitute record_id
column2: if an existing identifier has not yet been supplied, leave the field unfinished for completion.","Digit-only text, or N/A for no EPPI record. Real identifiers must be unique
column3: N/A may recur. Blank and NI prohibited in completed data."

column1: first_author,First-author surname or group-author label used for the study citation.,"Read the first author from the article byline. Preserve compound surnames, spelling, and diacritics. column2: blank, NI, and N/A prohibited."

column1: publication_year,Publication year of the included version of record.,"Read the year from the published article and its issue or publisher citation. Do not substitute an indexing, acceptance, PDF-filename, or online-first year for the included version-of-record year. Record any discrepancy in the evidence note.","Four digits

column1: article_title,Published title of the included article.,"Transcribe the title from the article, checking publisher metadata if needed. Preserve wording and punctuation, normalising whitespace only.","Text
column2: blank, NI, and N/A prohibited."

column1: study_design,"Design of the complete eligible investigation, independent of any selected efficacy result.","Apply the investigation boundary in extraction_instructions.md to every scientific field. Classify the complete allocation structure, arms, and periods. Parallel groups use different participants in separate groups, which may be non-concurrent. Cross-over assigns the same participants different conditions across periods. Pre-post is organised around a before-and-after intervention comparison. Single arm is an uncontrolled one-group intervention trial. Case report is a clinical account of individual patients. Longitudinal outcomes alone do not turn a nominal single-arm trial into Pre-post
column2: one uncontrolled group alone does not establish Single arm. Preserve allocation details in the evidence note. Use NI when the design cannot be established.","Values: Parallel groups
column3: Cross-over

column1: pain_measurements,Each distinct pain-related construct paired with its measurement scale or response-method family.,"Retain all eligible construct-method pairs, including descriptive measures that do not qualify for efficacy counts. Intensity is the amount of pain experienced
column2: Threshold is the stimulus level at which pain begins or reaches a defined point. For stimulus-threshold tests, record the participant response method, such as Verbal report or Button press, and keep apparatus and units in evidence. column3: that label applies to an explicitly force-defined pain-tolerance endpoint. Use a supported generic response method when the instrument name is unreported. Keep other constructs close to the source. column1: sample_size,Design-appropriate number of unique participants in the complete eligible investigation.,"For a randomised parallel or cross-over investigation, prefer the number randomised, established from an explicit total, participant flow, or complete allocation accounting. Only if that count cannot be established may an explicitly reported enrolled count for the same eligible investigation be used. For a non-random controlled investigation, count those allocated or enrolled at its start
column2: for a pre-post or single-arm investigation, those starting the eligible menthol intervention
column3: for a case report, the persons described. Count each person once across eligible arms, experiments, and periods
column4: count people, not clusters. Do not substitute screened, analysed, or completer counts. Include relevant eligible controls, but exclude people solely in a separable menthol pain-model reference component. A reference exposure on an eligible participant does not remove that person. Preserve total/component counts and their bases in evidence. Use NI if neither the governing count nor its permitted fallback is established.",Non-negative whole number or NI

column4: and persons_described for case reports. Assess the complete eligible allocation structure: randomisation of only a subset does not make all eligible conditions randomised. Determine the governing basis even when sample_size is NI
column5: for a randomised investigation with neither count established, retain randomised. Do not change the basis by adding a separate pain-model reference component.","Values: randomised

column1: menthol_concentration,"Every distinct reported or reproducibly convertible menthol percentage for eligible topical preparations, linked to the reported purpose of menthol.","Retain points, ranges, and reproducible conversions with their bases and qualifications. Preserve peppermint/product percentages without treating them as menthol percentages
column2: do not infer typical composition or invent range endpoints. Map each preparation to its concentration and menthol purpose before collapsing repeated identical values, bases, and qualifications. Therapeutic means intended or investigated as a therapeutic component, including in a comparator. Masking/control means menthol used for masking or a nominal placebo/control without a stated therapeutic role for that menthol
column3: it does not include every comparator. The instructions explain clinical pain-effect investigations and separation of pain-model reference components. Do not infer purpose from dose size or overall arm labels. Both requires evidence of both purposes for the same value, basis, and qualification, within or across preparations. Keep Both if both purposes are evidenced even when another represented purpose is unclear
column4: otherwise use purpose NI if any represented purpose remains unresolved. Preserve known purposes and preparation links in evidence. Unavailable concentration takes no tag and does not imply unknown purpose. Aggregate tags do not determine comparison eligibility. Retain masking/control preparations descriptively even when their findings are excluded.","Purpose labels: Therapeutic

Retain each site once, label inferences in evidence, and preserve uncertainty about extent without inventing wider coverage.","Concise text close to the source, with entries separated by '

column1: co_intervention,Each substantive outcome-relevant exposure delivered alongside menthol and common to the compared regimens in at least one eligible comparison.,"Remove the focal menthol and comparator components before deciding whether an exposure is common. Exclude inert masking/placebo components and additions confined to one arm. A shared trace masking component must be retained with its effect uncertain when the report explicitly raises a possible outcome contribution
column2: masking purpose alone does not establish inertness. Do not infer unreported ingredients. Record each named co-intervention once. Use N/A only when evidence establishes that none applies anywhere, and NI when one may apply but usable information is insufficient.",Concise named entries separated by '
column3: '. NI may stand alone or accompany named entries as bare NI or NI (<unresolved co-intervention>). Whole-cell N/A must stand alone.

column1: comparator,"Every distinct eligible comparator regimen, with its description, reported intended role, and controlled type linked in one entry.","Create one profile per distinct regimen. Collapse repetition across outcomes, models, times, or analyses, but retain distinct arms, formulations, doses, routes, timings, and scientifically distinct baseline occasions. Different measurement methods alone do not create different regimens. Classify the whole comparator relative to topical menthol after separating a genuinely shared substantive co-intervention, retaining that context in the description or evidence. Therapeutic denotes an intended or investigated therapeutic alternative
column2: Control denotes a nominal placebo/masking or listed reference condition. Neither proves activity or inactivity. Use source role and methods, not ingredient presence, dose size, or assumed effective thresholds. Menthol is a therapeutic type only when its role is therapeutic. Keep masking menthol in the description, including where another ingredient makes the comparator Therapeutic. A eucalyptus regimen with masking peppermint therefore retains Eucalyptus without automatically adding Menthol. Usual care is a reference condition, distinct from shared background care or a deliberately contrasted therapeutic alternative. Keep each multicomponent regimen together with all applicable therapeutic types. Whole-regimen role, menthol purpose, and comparison eligibility remain separate judgements. Preserve partial information, source limitations, and ingredients
column3: do not guess an unresolved role. Apply the investigation boundary and retain descriptive coverage even when a finding is ineligible.","Control types: Nominal placebo/masking

column1: Therapeutic types: Breast milk
column2: Heat
column3: Ice

column2: '. Partial examples: NI [Control: Nominal placebo/masking] or <description> [Therapeutic: NI]. Type NI stands alone within its profile. Whole-cell NI or a separate NI (<unresolved regimen>) is allowed
column3: bare NI cannot accompany known profiles. Whole-cell N/A means no eligible comparator and stands alone. Repeated profiles or types, including profiles with reordered types, are prohibited."

column1: efficacy_result_count,Confirmed minimum number of distinct explicitly reported eligible comparisons and descriptive case-report pain findings.,"Use the primary article and formal supplements. Apply the investigation, outcome, treatment-component, explicit-reporting, and grouping rules in extraction_instructions.md in that order, then count the confirmed inventory. Comparative wording, labels, annotations, or statistical results may establish a finding
column2: separate arm values or study design alone cannot. Significance, a numerical estimate, precision, and exact timing are not prerequisites. Count only eligible menthol/peppermint therapeutic-purpose findings, with the stated descriptive-case exception. Keep genuinely distinct findings
column3: group repeated presentations and alternative analyses of the same comparison. Preserve possible additions, uncertain duplication, source gaps, exclusions, and checking attempts in the evidence note. Retain confirmed positive counts despite uncertainty about additions. Use 0 only after adequate checking establishes none, and NI only when neither a confirmed positive count nor a supported zero is established. Missing estimates or precision do not remove a finding. A zero count does not mean no analgesic effect or an ineligible study. Inclusion does not establish causality.","Non-negative whole number or NI
column4: blank and N/A prohibited. A numeric value equals the confirmed grouped inventory size, including 0. Assess other fields independently."

column1: efficacy_effect_estimate_count,Confirmed number of counted comparisons with at least one usable reported or directly calculable effect estimate.,"Assess the same confirmed inventory and count each comparison once. A compatible reported analysis representation or supported direct calculation can establish availability but cannot create a comparison. Keep its inputs, units, population, occasion, formula, and source. Do not model, impute, digitise graphs, or assume unreported information. A p value, test statistic, direction, or qualitative statement alone is insufficient
column2: a numerical zero is an available estimate. Clearly labelled graphical contrast estimates count as reported without reading off their magnitudes or requiring printed numerical labels. Separate arm plots do not create comparisons. Missing precision does not remove an estimate. Retain confirmed availability despite unresolved entries
column3: use 0 only after adequate negative checking, and NI only when neither a positive count nor a supported zero is established. Use N/A for descriptive case reports, independently of their result count
column4: numerical observations or calculable changes may still be documented.","Non-negative whole number, NI, or descriptive-case-report N/A. Numeric count equals confirmed estimate-available inventory entries and cannot exceed a numeric efficacy_result_count. Case reports require N/A in both availability fields. Non-case result count 0 requires both availability counts 0
column5: estimate count 0 requires precision count 0. No automatic NI propagation. Blank prohibited."

column1: efficacy_effect_estimate_with_precision_count,"Confirmed number of counted comparisons with a usable estimate and its matching, design-appropriate precision.","Count a comparison once when one permitted analysis representation supplies both its estimate and matching confidence interval, standard error, or variance, reported or directly calculable from compatible information. Match analysis, effect, population, occasion, and design
column2: do not exchange estimates and intervals between final/change or adjusted/unadjusted analyses. No modelling, imputation, graph digitisation, or unreported assumptions. Separate arm/time-point standard deviations alone do not supply paired-change or crossover precision
column3: a p value alone is insufficient, and omnibus tests cannot supply individual-contrast precision. Retain unusable-interval limitations without deleting the comparison or available estimate. This assesses information availability, not general risk of bias or preferred estimates for synthesis. Retain confirmed availability despite uncertain additions
column4: use 0 after adequate negative checking and NI only when neither a positive count nor a supported zero is established. Every precision-qualified comparison must have an available estimate. Apply the further safeguards in extraction_instructions.md.","Non-negative whole number, NI, or descriptive-case-report N/A. Where numeric, precision <= estimates <= results
column5: positive precision requires positive confirmed estimate and result counts. In non-case studies, result count 0 or estimate count 0 requires precision 0. No automatic NI cascade. N/A is required in both availability fields together for descriptive case reports, independently of their result count. Blank prohibited."

column1: study_registration,Public study-registration status and timing relative to first participant enrolment.,"Follow the documented registry-search procedure in extraction_instructions.md. Match using identifiers, title, intervention, investigators, sites, dates, and sample characteristics. Prefer the first submission date. Prospective means registration before the supported first-enrolment period
column2: Retrospective means after enrolment began or explicitly while recruiting. Preserve partial-date uncertainty. Use the qualified no-match label after the documented search, never as proof that registration did not occur. Use NI when a match exists but timing is unresolved or the search cannot establish classification.","Values: Prospective
column3: Retrospective
column4: No sufficiently matched public registry record located

column1: One value. Blank and N/A prohibited."

adverse_event_reporting,"Study-level adverse-event reporting across all eligible topical-menthol groups and exposure periods, including combination treatments.","Check adverse events, tolerability, and relevant withdrawal or treatment-change information in the primary article and formal supplements. Events reported means any documented event during eligible menthol exposure, regardless of attribution, and overrides negative statements. Explicitly no events reported requires a clear overall zero covering relevant menthol groups and the reported observation period without contradictory events. Use Limited or unclear information for tolerability-only, event-specific or treatment-related-only negatives, incomplete coverage, conflicts, uncertain exposure timing, or comparator-only reporting. Use NI only when no relevant information is identified. Ordinary planned pain outcomes are not automatically adverse events
column2: general pharmacological background is not participant safety reporting. Non-adherence or withdrawal without a reported health-related reason is not itself adverse-event information.","Values: Events reported
column3: Explicitly no events reported

column1: One value. Blank and N/A prohibited, including case reports."

adverse_event_details,"Concise account of adverse-event information and its treatment, population, and observation scope.","Summarise relevant events, negative or qualified statements, and conflicts. Label different menthol regimens, combination treatments, periods, and comparator-only information. Retain reported event types, numbers, units/denominators, timing, withdrawals or treatment changes, and investigator attribution. Do not invent counts, rates, denominators, causality, or broader negative findings. Do not substitute overall sample size for an unstated safety denominator.","Readable text, usually a few sentences, or NI. NI if and only if adverse_event_reporting is NI
column2: every other status requires substantive details. Blank and N/A prohibited."
